What to know before using Jetpac eSIM for Japan

Before you travel, here are a few important things to know so your Jetpac eSIM works smoothly:

Data & Voice Packs

Jetpac eSIM provides 4G/5G connection, multi-network support and unlimited hotspot. Voice packs allows you to call any number across 50+ countries starting from $1.99 for 5 minutes.

eSIM compatibility

Your phone must support eSIM and be unlocked. Double-check your eSIM compatibility before purchasing.

Activation timing

Install your eSIM when you buy it, but only activate it after landing. This way you avoid early expiry.

Keep your primary SIM

With dual-SIM functionality, you can keep your own number active for calls/texts while Jetpac handles your data.

eSIM Travel Tips You Should Know for Japan

Activate after arrival

Install before you fly. Switch on your eSIM once you have landed so your mobile data plans lasts for your full trip.

Manage multiple SIMs seamlessly

Jetpac eSIM works alongside your primary SIM for mobile data and voice packs.

Monitor your usage

Manage your data usage on the Jetpac Global app and top up on the go. Never run out unexpectedly.

Frequently asked questions

A travel eSIM is a digital SIM built into your phone that lets you activate a local or regional mobile plan abroad without needing a physical SIM card. You simply download the eSIM via QR code or app, and your phone connects to the local network for data, calls, and texts. With an eSIM there will be no more roaming charges. Travel eSIMs are popular with frequent flyers because you can store multiple plans, switch between countries easily, and avoid paying high roaming fees.

You can purchase an eSIM online from an eSIM provider. After purchase, you’ll receive a QR code or activation details by email.

Prices vary by destination and data amount; many destination pages start “from US$1”. Check the specific Japan page for the latest rates to avoid roaming fees.

Often Yes. Using a local or regional eSIM is usually much cheaper as it provides affordable pricing than international roaming charges.

Usually no. One eSIM profile can hold multiple data plans; you can add/remove plans as you travel. With Jetpac specifically, you can keep the same eSIM and just buy another pack later. This will ensure you get high speed internet with fast and reliable coverage while ensuring affordable pricing

The best option depends on your data needs, travel duration, network support (5G/4G) and device compatibility. Compare providers for coverage and cost. Jetpac data plans are usually 70% cheaper than roaming charges. It provides reliable connectivity, reliable coverage, prepaid eSIM plans and options for you to get unlimited internet- making Jetpac the best travel eSIM for Europe.

To activate an eSIM, simply scan the QR code or follow the instructions sent by your provider; install the eSIM on your phone before you travel, then once you arrive in Japan, enable Data Roaming on that eSIM line so it can connect to the local network and activate automatically.

You can access your eSIM immediately after purchase through an email sent by us. With the eSIM, you can enjoy your trip with fast and reliable internet connection and without any roaming fees or charges.

Yes, it’s best to install your eSIM at home while connected to Wi-Fi, so it’s ready on your device and you can connect instantly when you arrive in Japan.

Yes, turn on Data Roaming for the travel eSIM line so it can register on partner networks.

You can extend your eSIM with the Jetpac website or app, where you can top-up within a few clicks and stay connected without roaming fees.

If your data runs out or your plan expires, you’ll need to buy a new plan or top-up for reliable connection and seamless experience. Jetpac still gives you free access to essential apps like Uber, WhatsApp, Grab, and Google Maps.

Yes, if your device supports hotspot or tethering. Jetpac allows unlimited tethering with no data cap, so you can stay connected with your other devices and even share data with your loved ones through hotspot.

Jetpac wants to ensure, our users get their international eSIM for Europe with the most-optimum usage and most affordable prices.

Providers partner with local carriers, and your eSIM will connect to one of those networks, often with 4G or 5G, ensuring reliable connection. Jetpac clearly lists the supported networks and their types (4G/5G) for each specific data plan, based on local network coverage.

Most travel eSIMs are data-only, which means you can only make calls and send texts through apps like WhatsApp, Skype, or Messenger. Jetpac goes further by offering outgoing calls to 50+ countries starting from just $1.99 for 5 minutes, giving you a more flexible option when you need a direct call.

Yes. WhatsApp works with your original number, regardless of which SIM you use for data.

Yes, leave your physical SIM active for voice/SMS and set your international travel eSIM for Japan.

Most travel eSIMs are data-only but Jetpac offers voice calling packs which are affordable and provide reliable connection.

An international travel eSIM for Japan does not drain more battery than a normal SIM. The battery use for a travel eSIM for Japan is similar.

An eSIM gives you fast setup with no store queues, instant activation on landing, easy top-ups, and the flexibility to keep your home number active for calls and SMS. Unlike other providers, only Jetpac goes further by giving you free SmartDelay lounge access if your flight is delayed, so you can stay comfortable while you wait. With a Jetpac eSIM there will be no more roaming charges or bill shocks- just high-speed and reliable internet connection.

What is Travel eSIM and how does it work?
A travel eSIM is a digital SIM built into your phone that lets you activate a local or regional mobile plan abroad without needing a physical SIM card. You simply download the eSIM via QR code or app, and your phone connects to the local network for data, calls, and texts. With an eSIM there will be no more roaming charges. Travel eSIMs are popular with frequent flyers because you can store multiple plans, switch between countries easily, and avoid paying high roaming fees.
How can I get an eSIM for Japan?
You can purchase an eSIM online from an eSIM provider. After purchase, you’ll receive a QR code or activation details by email.

Is an eSIM cheaper than roaming in Japan?
Often Yes. Using a local or regional eSIM is usually much cheaper as it provides affordable pricing than international roaming charges.
Do I need a separate eSIM for each Japan country?
Usually no. One eSIM profile can hold multiple data plans; you can add/remove plans as you travel. With Jetpac specifically, you can keep the same eSIM and just buy another pack later. This will ensure you get high speed internet with fast and reliable coverage while ensuring affordable pricing

How do I activate an eSIM for Japan?
To activate an eSIM, simply scan the QR code or follow the instructions sent by your provider; install the eSIM on your phone before you travel, then once you arrive in Japan, enable Data Roaming on that eSIM line so it can connect to the local network and activate automatically.
When will I receive my eSIM?
You can access your eSIM immediately after purchase through an email sent by us. With the eSIM, you can enjoy your trip with fast and reliable internet connection and without any roaming fees or charges.
Should I install my eSIM before I travel?
Yes, it’s best to install your eSIM at home while connected to Wi-Fi, so it’s ready on your device and you can connect instantly when you arrive in Japan.
Do I have to enable data roaming for my eSIM to work?
Yes, turn on Data Roaming for the travel eSIM line so it can register on partner networks.
Will an eSIM work on my phone or tablet?
Most recent iPhone, Samsung, Google Pixel, and newer tablets support eSIM. Check your device’s settings and compatibility to confirm.
Does my phone need to be unlocked to use an eSIM?
Yes. Your device must be unlocked to use an eSIM from another provider.
Can I use my physical SIM card and eSIM at the same time?
Yes, many devices support dual SIM (one physical SIM + one eSIM).
When does my mobile data plan begin?
The plan starts once you activate the eSIM or connect to the local network.
Can I extend or renew my eSIM data plan?
You can extend your eSIM with the Jetpac website or app, where you can top-up within a few clicks and stay connected without roaming fees.
What happens if I run out of data or days of validity?
If your data runs out or your plan expires, you’ll need to buy a new plan or top-up for reliable connection and seamless experience. Jetpac still gives you free access to essential apps like Uber, WhatsApp, Grab, and Google Maps.
Can I share data with other devices (hotspot/tethering)?
Yes, if your device supports hotspot or tethering. Jetpac allows unlimited tethering with no data cap, so you can stay connected with your other devices and even share data with your loved ones through hotspot.
How can I check my data balance?
Jetpac wants to ensure, our users get their international eSIM for Europe with the most-optimum usage and most affordable prices.
Which mobile networks will I connect to in Japan?
Providers partner with local carriers, and your eSIM will connect to one of those networks, often with 4G or 5G, ensuring reliable connection. Jetpac clearly lists the supported networks and their types (4G/5G) for each specific data plan, based on local network coverage.
Can I make calls and send SMS with an eSIM?
Most travel eSIMs are data-only, which means you can only make calls and send texts through apps like WhatsApp, Skype, or Messenger. Jetpac goes further by offering outgoing calls to 50+ countries starting from just $1.99 for 5 minutes, giving you a more flexible option when you need a direct call.
Can I keep my WhatsApp number with an eSIM?
Yes. WhatsApp works with your original number, regardless of which SIM you use for data.
Can I still use my regular phone number with an eSIM?
Yes, leave your physical SIM active for voice/SMS and set your international travel eSIM for Japan.
Are there any disadvantages to using an eSIM in Japan?

Does an international travel eSIM for Japan drain more battery than a local SIM?
